title: Mab, Queen of Courts
subtitle: Glamour & Bargain

lore.description: Mab, the Hazel Queen, rules not from throne or blade, but from dance and debt. She is the smile that binds, the jest that ensnares, the hostess who makes guests complicit in her game. To speak in her Court is to pay; to receive her token is to owe. Mab is an Archfae — one of the great powers of the Gloaming Courts, neither wholly cruel nor kind, but always bound by her own rules. She cannot lie, but she can mislead so beautifully that truth becomes irrelevant. She cannot break an oath, but she can interpret it until it screams.
lore.followers: Her followers thrive on charm, wit, and story, spreading webs of bargains too subtle to escape. The Cantor's Path sings her name most sweetly, for every verse carries a price. Among the peoples of Fate's Edge, Mab is the patron of courtiers, actors, and those who live by their wits. In Aelinnel, she is the Unbounded Guest, whose arrival at a feast is marked by laughter and shattered glass — and a new debt for the host. In Vilikari salons, she is the Gilded Tongue, invoked before every negotiation. Wherever masks are worn and words have double meanings, Mab watches.
lore.quote: Every laugh is a promise. Every promise is a debt. Every debt belongs to Mab.

domain_focus: Fae Glamour: illusions, enchantments, the art of seeming
Social Bargains: oaths, promises, debt as social glue
Courtly Intrigue: etiquette, wordplay, the game of masks
Trickster Arts: mischief, cleverness, the twist in the tale

thiasos.description: A Runekeeper who serves Mab does not bind a familiar of raw power. Their Thiasos is a small creature of glamour and wit: a talking cricket that gives advice in riddles, a cat with mismatched eyes that appears at masquerades, a small fox that steals shiny baubles and leaves cryptic notes, a white jay that mimics voices with uncanny accuracy, or a spider that weaves its web in the shape of a courtly dance.
thiasos.care: This creature requires no food, but it must witness a promise or a performance each day. If neglected for a week, it becomes Compromised (it pulls pranks at the worst moments — tugging a sleeve during a lie, knocking over a wine glass — imposing –1 die on all Deception and Performance rolls for its bearer until it next witnesses a genuine oath).

codex.description: You will not find Mab's Codex bound as a book of straightforward text. It may be a deck of playing cards whose suits shift when no one is looking, a mirror that reflects only the backs of words, a set of silk handkerchiefs knotted into a puzzle, or a scroll that must be read while dancing.
codex.upkeep: Because Mab's truths are written in misdirection, the Codex requires upkeep: the Runekeeper must spend an hour each week re-ordering the cards (or re-knotting the handkerchiefs) while recounting a story from memory, or the patterns become scrambled (treat as Compromised until re-woven).

patrons_gift.name: Mab's Jest
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of Mab may touch a held item (weapon, tool, or garment) and whisper a jest.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, the item grants +1 die to Deception or Performance rolls, and the first time each scene the bearer would be caught in a lie, they may roll Deception again (the glamour twists the truth).
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to Mab.

rites.name: Rite of the Trickster's Bargain
rites.materials: A token freely given (flower, coin, ribbon).
rites.effect: Offer a fae bargain. The target may accept (both gain +1 die to actions that uphold the terms) or refuse (target marks 1 Fatigue from social pressure).
rites.push_it: If the target later betrays the bargain, they suffer Harm 1 (Stress) and start an Oathbreaker [4] timer. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of Courtly Guise
rites.materials: A sprig of hawthorn or a silver thread worn visibly.
rites.effect: Subtle glamour makes you appear as the expected rank or guest. Gain +1 die to social rolls in refined settings.
rites.push_it: Mask one personal tell (an accent, a scar, a nervous habit); the first probing question about it generates 1 SB (Hearts). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Price Agreed
rites.materials: Equal tokens exchanged ritually (two rings, two signed notes, two locks of hair).
rites.effect: Bind a formal bargain. While the bargain is honored, both parties gain +1 Effect when cooperating. Breach forces 1 SB (Hearts/Diamonds) and a reputation penalty (–1 die to social rolls involving honor for one week).
rites.push_it: Add a minor boon to one party (+1 die once). If that party breaches, they suffer an additional 1 SB and you mark +1 Obligation. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Sovereign Glamour
rites.materials: A circle of silk or green felt, courtly music, and a drop of honey and vinegar.
rites.effect: Establish a fae court in the zone. For the scene: allies gain +1 die to social rolls; blunt threats (Intimidation, crude Force) suffer –1 die. Once per scene, strip an illusion or reveal a hidden motive as a free action (target tests Resolve DV 3). Violating a promise made within the zone triggers 2 SB and a visible glamour mark (a blush, a stutter) lasting a day.
rites.push_it: Impose a temporary Court Law (e.g., 'no steel,' 'speak only truth,' 'every third word must be a compliment'). Violators suffer 2 SB. Cost: Mark +2 Obligation (total +4) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Gilded Jest
rites.materials: Hand-made masks for all participants, enchanted music, and a cup of wine blessed (or cursed) with a whispered lie.
rites.effect: Create a lasting glamoured court — a masquerade that persists for the duration of the event. All social magic (Sway, Performance, Deception) gains +1 Effect. Outsiders who enter suffer –1 die to perceive truths, read emotions, or see through disguises. Any promise made while masked is magically witnessed; breaking it inflicts 2 SB and the mask of the oath-breaker cracks (visible to all).
rites.push_it: The masquerade persists between scenes for the rest of the session. Cost: Mark +3 Obligation (total +5) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of Mab sings in harmonies of the half-truth — melodies that shift key without warning, leaving the listener uncertain of what was heard. Their voice is used to seal a bargain with a sung clause, to make a crowd forget a social faux pas, or to weave a glamour that lasts as long as the music plays. Mab's Cantors are prized at every court where masks are worn, and feared by those who know that a beautiful tune can hide a poisoned promise.

cult.name: The Cult of the Gilded Jest
cult.description: Mab's cults meet in places where masks are natural: masquerade balls, carnival tents, and the back rooms of theaters. The Gilded Jest is less a religion and more a conspiracy of wits — actors, gamblers, and lawyers who have learned that every exchange is a performance. A ritual of the Jest involves each member writing a true secret on a playing card, then exchanging cards with another member. They must then speak the secret they received as if it were their own — and the group votes on whether they told it 'true enough.' Those who fail must drink a cup of 'tea of forgotten clauses' and lose one minor memory (a face, a password, a small debt). Their creed is printed on a card that is passed, never kept: 'The best chains are made of laughter. The strongest oaths are sworn in jest.' Outsiders are welcome as 'audience,' but those who laugh too loudly may find themselves on stage — and the stage has its own rules.

witchcraft.name: The Art of Glamour and Toy
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with Mab is a glamour-weaver or toy-maker — one who crafts objects that are never quite what they seem. Their magic works through misdirection: a doll that laughs when a promise is broken, a mirror that shows a flattering reflection (and nothing else), or a mask that lets the wearer speak any lie as truth. Their tools are never hammers; they use needles, masks, and the subtle art of a well-placed reflection. In Aeler, a True-Mason might carve a cornerstone that makes everyone forget the building's weak point, but a witch of Mab would instead sew a glamour seam into the cornerstone's shadow.
witchcraft.lore: The glamour-weaver's path is the art of seeming. They learn that a well-told lie is a kindness as often as a weapon, that a mask worn honestly reveals more than a bare face, and that every party has a hostess who is owed a favor by morning. Mab's witches keep court in miniature — a table, a deck of cards, a room full of guests who do not yet know what they have agreed to.
witchcraft.quote: Wear the mask well, and no one will ask what it hides.

mask_of_shifting_faces.name: The Mask of Shifting Faces
mask_of_shifting_faces.description: A simple half-mask of polished white wood, its eye holes rimmed with silver. Once per session, the witch may don the mask and change their apparent appearance — face, voice, and even perceived gender — for one scene. This grants +2 dice to Deception or Performance rolls to pass as someone else, and anyone who tries to see through the disguise must test Resolve (DV 4). The mask cannot mimic a specific person unless the witch has a token of that person. After use, the mask's eyes weep a single drop of silver; the witch may collect it as a component for glamour rites.

hedge_gifts.name: Mask of the Moment
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, the witch may place a hand over their own face and draw it away, revealing a different expression (or a different face entirely, briefly). This grants +1 die to a single Deception or Performance roll, as the target's expectations are momentarily overturned. The illusion lasts only for that exchange.

hedge_gifts.name: Fair Trade
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, when you offer someone a small, freely-given gift, they gain +1 die on their next roll — but they also owe you a genuine favor, of a scope you name aloud. Refusing the gift after it is offered costs them 1 Fatigue (the sting of a slighted host).

hedge_gifts.name: Toymaker's Trick
hedge_gifts.description: You may craft a small enchanted toy (a doll, a puzzle box, a wind-up bird) during downtime. Once, it can trigger a minor, specific effect you set when you made it — laughing at a lie, weeping at a broken promise, or unlocking at a spoken word. Requires an hour of quiet work and a personal token.

monastic_tradition.name: The Way of the Hollow Crown
monastic_tradition.description: Monks of the Hollow Crown study Mab's rules the way a duelist studies a blade — not to break them, but to find the gap between the letter and the intent. They speak precisely, bow correctly, and never once tell a plain lie, yet leave every negotiation having given away nothing and gained everything. Their training is as much etiquette as combat: how to hold a room, how to make silence cost more than words, how to let an opponent's own oath become the trap.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Presence 3+, Wits 2+, Rite of Courtly Guise or Cantor of Mab.
monastic_tradition.quote: Bow to no one you cannot outlast at the table.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: The Hollow Crown teaches that a debt is only as binding as its wording. Monks gain +1 die to resist or reinterpret a social debt, favor, or promise extracted from them under pressure or deception, so long as they can point to a technicality in how it was framed. If they succeed, the obligation holds in form but loses its teeth — everyone at the table knows it, and no one can prove it.

basic.name: Courtier's Poise
basic.description: Once per scene, when insulted, threatened, or provoked in a social setting, you may respond with a composed retort instead of reacting; gain +1 die to your next social roll against that provocateur.

advanced.name: Read the Room
advanced.description: Once per scene, spend a moment observing a gathering to learn who holds real power, who is lying, and who owes whom a debt (GM answers one question per category, in riddle if warranted).

master.name: The Uncrowned Verdict
master.description: Once per session, declare a social 'ruling' within a scene you dominate — a judgment, a decree, a verdict on who owes what to whom. Those present who accept it (even tacitly, by not objecting) are bound to it as if it were a formal bargain for the rest of the scene.

corruption.benefit: Glamour's Touch: +1 die to Deception/Performance with stories.
corruption.cost: Truthbound: Cannot speak plain falsehood; only mislead.

corruption.benefit: Fairy Step: Once per scene, flicker Near as if teleporting.
corruption.cost: Iron Weakness: 1 Fatigue if touched by cold iron.

corruption.benefit: Trickster's Delight: Spend 1 Boon to twist a Complication advantageously.
corruption.cost: Compulsive Jest: Must play a trick each session or mark 1 SB.

corruption.benefit: Hospitality's Gift: Allies sharing food/drink gain +1 die to Resolve.
corruption.cost: Hospitality Bound: Harming guests costs +2 Obligation.

corruption.benefit: Fae Sight: See veils/glamours; +2 dice to Notice.
corruption.cost: Truth Debt: Must accept 'fair' trades or suffer.

corruption.benefit: Twilight Crown: Once/session, declare an Oath; you gain +2 dice to all rolls that fulfill it, and enemies who swore the same oath suffer –1 die to resist its terms.
corruption.cost: Oathbound: Breaking this oath inflicts Harm 2 (Stress) and starts an Iron Debt [6] timer that can only be cleared by a quest. Your shadow is now forked — a visible sign that Mab has marked you.

playstyle_notes.description: Mab excels in social manipulation and fae-style bargaining. Followers become masters of subtle magic, binding others through oaths and glamour. The corruption progression leads toward becoming fae-touched, gaining power over truth and perception at the cost of mortal constraints. Intrusions often take the form of a forgotten bargain resurfacing, a guest demanding hospitality you cannot refuse, or a jest that turns cruel. Ideal for players who enjoy social intrigue, wordplay, and characters who prefer cleverness over brute force.
emphasizes: Archfae Sovereignty: Mab's word is law in her presence, but only if you play her game
Glamour as Social Weapon: illusions that bind, masks that deceive
Bargains and Debts: every gift is a hook, every promise a leash
Courtly Intrigue: etiquette, wordplay, the dance of masks
Trickster Wisdom: the truth is what you can make others believe

sample_adventure.title: The Guest Who Would Not Leave
sample_adventure.description: A minor noble has thrown a masquerade in Mab's honor, hoping to curry favor before a contested inheritance. An uninvited guest arrived at midnight, laughing, and has not left — nor has anyone been able to make them. Every attempt to eject them results in an accident, a scandal, or a forgotten obligation surfacing at the worst moment. The party is hired to end the impasse, but Mab's guest cannot simply be removed: they must be out-bargained, out-witted, or given exactly what the Court decides they are owed.
sample_adventure.quote: You did not read the invitation closely enough. No one ever does. That is rather the point.
